digest.component_or_area: plan-review: AC satisfiability criterion and child-coverage audit
propositions: Plan review certifies tickets with mutually unsatisfiable acceptance criteria across parent and children without detecting the contradiction in Pass-1, forcing re-review at later gates when the material becomes stale-marked.

A new 1-TURN criterion `ac-satisfiability` (facet `coherence`, advisory 0.95) must detect three shapes of within-description quantifier conflicts: universal-vs-carve-out, derived-artifact closure, and snapshot cardinality, none of which COH, E1, or F1 owns today.

G3's child-coverage audit cannot fire because the sibling roster it receives carries only child ids and titles; it must receive each child's acceptance-criteria items extracted via `evaluate_plan_clarity(...).ac_items` to discharge the no-sibling-covers-it test.

The sibling roster expression is duplicated in three non-test locations (pass1.py:154, fidelity_spot_eval.py:219, eval_solver.py:117-119) and must be single-sourced via a shared `build_sibling_roster` helper to prevent eval harnesses from sending title-only rosters while production sends AC-bearing ones, which would corrupt dogfooding data.

The roster must move from per-pairing instructions into the byte-stable system prompt prefix to be rendered once per review rather than once per child pairing, and its token cost must be included in the `parent_tokens` estimate that gates bin-packing and the warm-then-fan-out cache threshold.
G3's posture, threshold, and ownership boundary remain unchanged; Pass-2's `internal_conflict` verifier axis already grades this defect, so no review-kernel changes are in scope.
